title: Advancing parser step
statement: Let $b_s,\alpha,x,\mathrm{clock},\mathrm{out}$ be Boolean words, let $q$ be a parser control state, let $q'$ be an optional parser control state, and let $e$ be an optional Boolean output. Suppose $p$ is a position strictly before the end of the nested pair encoding $\langle\langle b_s,\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, and its bit at position $p$ is $b$. If, for every work-tape reading, the parser in state $q$ on input bit $b$ moves right, leaves its work tape unchanged, emits $e$, and enters $q'$, then from the configuration at input position $p+1$, with clock buffer $\mathrm{clock}$ and output $\mathrm{out}$, one step reaches the configuration at position $p+2$, with the same clock buffer and output $\mathrm{out}$ followed by $e$; the state is $q'$.
hypotheses_covered: Position $p$ is below the encoding length
For every work-tape reading, the transition on $b$ in state $q$ is rightward, writes nothing, emits $e$, and enters $q'$
replaced:
Suppose the prefix parser's transition in control $q$, on the input symbol
found at physical position $p$ of the nested pair encoding, moves the input
head right, writes nothing to the work tape, optionally emits one bit, and
passes to a control $q'$.  Then one machine step from the corresponding parser
configuration advances the physical input position by one, appends the
optional emission to the output, keeps the stored clock unchanged, and enters
$q'$.
